title: Zariski's main theorem, global affine form: a quasi-finite finite type algebra is open in a finite subalgebra of its integral closure (Stacks 00QB)
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a ring map of finite type such that $R\to S$ is quasi-finite at every prime ideal $\mathfrak q\subset S$ [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime], and let $S'\subseteq S$ be the integral closure of $R$ in $S$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. For a subring $T\subseteq S$ containing $\varphi(R)$ write $\operatorname{Spec}S\to\operatorname{Spec}T$ for the morphism of affine schemes [def-weil-affine-spectrum] induced by the inclusion $T\subseteq S$ (on points $\mathfrak q\mapsto\mathfrak q\cap T$); for $g\in T$ write $D(g)=\{\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}T:\ g\notin\mathfrak p\}$, and $T_g\to S_g$, $t/g^n\mapsto t/g^n$, for the map between the localizations of $T$ and of $S$ at the powers of $g$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away] induced by the inclusion. Then: (1) $\operatorname{Spec}S\to\operatorname{Spec}S'$ is a homeomorphism onto an open subset of $\operatorname{Spec}S'$; (2) if $g\in S'$ and $D(g)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}S'$ is contained in the image of $\operatorname{Spec}S\to\operatorname{Spec}S'$, then $S'_g\to S_g$ is an isomorphism; (3) there is a subring $S''\subseteq S'$ containing $\varphi(R)$ which is a finitely generated $R$-module via $\varphi$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] such that (1) and (2) hold with $S''$ in place of $S'$, and such that the morphism $\operatorname{Spec}S\to\operatorname{Spec}S''$ is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00QB (lemma-quasi-finite-open-integral-closure), line 30905, with its proof (lines 30920-30950); the open-immersion clause of (3) is the reformulation of (1) and (2) for $S''$ made in the proof of Morphisms, Lemma Tag 03GU (lemma-quasi-finite-affine), morphisms.tex line 15230
